                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### Anatomy of a Policy\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'Each policy defined in a resource has two parts -\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'- a condition or a list of conditions, such as `action_type(:read)`, `[action_type(:read), actor_attribute_equals(:admin, true)]` or `always()`. If the condition, or all conditions if given a list are true for a given action request, then the policy will be applied to the request.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'- a set of policy checks, each of which will be evaluated individually if a policy applies to a request.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'If more than one policy applies to any given request (eg. an admin actor calls a read action) then **all applicable policies must pass** for the action to be performed.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'A policy will produce one of three results: `:forbidden`, `:authorized`, or `:unknown`. `:unknown` is treated the same as `:forbidden`.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### The Simplest Policy\n'[39m +

                    [32m'  end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'The first argument to `policy` is the condition. In this case, the condition is `always()` - a built-in helper always returning true, meaning that the policy applies to every request.'[39m,

                    [32m'# Routing\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'AshJsonApi provides a set of route helpers that map HTTP requests to Ash actions. Routes are defined inside the `json_api do routes do ... end end` block on either a resource or a domain.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'## Route overview\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'| Route Helper | HTTP Method | Default Path | Primary Action Type | Also Accepts |\n'[39m +
                    [32m'|---|---|---|---|---|\n'[39m +
                    [32m'| `get` | GET | `/:id` | `:read` | `:action` |\n'[39m +
                    [32m'| `index` | GET | `/` | `:read` | `:action` |\n'[39m +
                    [32m'| `post` | POST | `/` | `:create` | `:action`, `:read` |\n'[39m +
                    [32m'| `patch` | PATCH | `/:id` | `:update` | `:action` |\n'[39m +
                    [32m'| `delete` | DELETE | `/:id` | `:destroy` | `:action` |\n'[39m +
                    [32m'| `related` | GET | `/:id/<relationship>` | `:read` | — |\n'[39m +
                    [32m'| `relationship` | GET | `/:id/relationships/<relationship>` | `:read` | — |\n'[39m +
                    [32m'| `post_to_relationship` | POST | `/:id/relationships/<relationship>` | `:update` | — |\n'[39m +
                    [32m'| `patch_relationship` | PATCH | `/:id/relationships/<relationship>` | `:update` | — |\n'[39m +
                    [32m'| `delete_from_relationship` | DELETE | `/:id/relationships/<relationship>` | `:update` | — |\n'[39m +
                    [32m'| `route` | *any* | *required* | `:action` | — |\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'## Defining routes\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'Routes can live on the resource or on the domain. Defining them on the domain is the default recommendation — it keeps resources focused on data and actions while the domain acts as the API surface.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### On the domain\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'defmodule MyApp.Support do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  use Ash.Domain, extensions: [AshJsonApi.Domain]\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  json_api do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    routes do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      base_route "/tickets", MyApp.Support.Ticket do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        get :read\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        index :read\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        post :create\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        patch :update\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        delete :destroy\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'`base_route` scopes all nested routes under the given path prefix for the specified resource.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### On the resource\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'defmodule MyApp.Support.Ticket do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  use Ash.Resource, extensions: [AshJsonApi.Resource]\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  json_api do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    type "ticket"\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    routes do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      base "/tickets"\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      get :read\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      index :read\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      post :create\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      patch :update\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      delete :destroy\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'`base` sets the path prefix for all routes defined on the resource.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'## Standard CRUD routes\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### `get` — fetch a single record\n'[39m +

                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### `index` — list records\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'index :read\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +

                    [32m'Options:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'- `paginate?` (default `true`) — whether to apply pagination\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### `post` — create a record\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +

                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'You can specify which arguments will modify relationships using `relationship_arguments`, but there are some things to keep in mind.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +

                    [32m'If you are not focused on building a fully compliant JSON:API, it is likely far simpler to simply accept arguments\n'[39m +
                    [32m'in the `attributes` key and ignore the `data.relationships` input.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m"If the argument's type is `{:array, _}`, a list of data will be expected. Otherwise, it will expect a single item.\n"[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'Everything in this guide applies to routs defined on the domain as well.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'For example:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'# On a tweets resource\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +

                    [32m'    patch :update, relationship_arguments: [:authors]\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'# And an argument by that name in the action\n'[39m +
                    [32m'actions do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  update :update do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    argument :authors, {:array, :map}, allow_nil?: false\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    change manage_relationship(:authors, type: :append_and_remove) # Use the authors argument to allow changing the related authors on update\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'You can then send the value for `authors` in the relationships key, e.g\n'[39m +

                    [32m'```json\n'[39m +
                    [32m'{\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  data: {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    attributes: {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      ...\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    },\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    relationships: {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      authors: {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        data: [\n'[39m +
                    [32m'          {type: "author", id: 1}, // the `type` key is removed when the value is placed into the action, so this input would be `%{"id" => 1}` (`type` is required by `JSON:API` specification)\n'[39m +
                    [32m'          {type: "author", id: 2, meta: {arbitrary: 1, keys: 2}}, <- `meta` is JSON:API spec freeform data, so this input would be `%{"id" => 2, "arbitrary" => 1, "keys" => 2}`\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        ]\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      }\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    }\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                    [32m'}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +

                    [32m'{\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  data: {\n'[39m +

                    [32m'      authors: {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        {id: 1},\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        {id: 2, arbitrary: 1, keys: 2},\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      }\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    }\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                    [32m'}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'Non-map argument types, e.g `argument :author, :integer` (expecting an author id) work with `manage_relationship`, but not with\n'[39m +
                    [32m'JSON:API, because it expects `{"type": _type, "id" => id}` for relationship values. To support non-map arguments in `relationship_arguments`,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'instead of `:author`, use `{:id, :author}`. This works for `{:array, _}` type arguments as well, so the value would be a list of ids.\n'[39m +

                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'## Creating related resources without the id\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'This feature is useful for creating relationships without requiring two separate API calls and without needing to associate resources with an ID first.                     [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +

                    [32m'# the API\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  json_api do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    routes do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      base_route "/location", Marketplace.Location do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        post :create, relationship_arguments: [:leads]\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      base_route "/lead", Marketplace.Lead do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        post :create\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'# In the leads resource you will have the following:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  actions do\n'[39m +

                    [32m'  # use `patch_relationship` when the operation is both additive and subtractive\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  # use `delete_from_relationship` when the operation is subtractive\n'[39m +
                    [32m'end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +

                    [32m'  change manage_relationship(:author, type: :append)\n'[39m +

                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'# Routing\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'AshJsonApi provides a set of route helpers that map HTTP requests to Ash actions. Routes are defined inside the `json_api do routes do ... end end` block on either a resource or a domain.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'## Route overview\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'| Route Helper | HTTP Method | Default Path | Primary Action Type | Also Accepts |\n'[39m +
                    [32m'|---|---|---|---|---|\n'[39m +
                    [32m'| `get` | GET | `/:id` | `:read` | `:action` |\n'[39m +
                    [32m'| `index` | GET | `/` | `:read` | `:action` |\n'[39m +
                    [32m'| `post` | POST | `/` | `:create` | `:action`, `:read` |\n'[39m +
                    [32m'| `patch` | PATCH | `/:id` | `:update` | `:action` |\n'[39m +
                    [32m'| `delete` | DELETE | `/:id` | `:destroy` | `:action` |\n'[39m +
                    [32m'| `related` | GET | `/:id/<relationship>` | `:read` | — |\n'[39m +
                    [32m'| `relationship` | GET | `/:id/relationships/<relationship>` | `:read` | — |\n'[39m +
                    [32m'| `post_to_relationship` | POST | `/:id/relationships/<relationship>` | `:update` | — |\n'[39m +
                    [32m'| `patch_relationship` | PATCH | `/:id/relationships/<relationship>` | `:update` | — |\n'[39m +
                    [32m'| `delete_from_relationship` | DELETE | `/:id/relationships/<relationship>` | `:update` | — |\n'[39m +
                    [32m'| `route` | *any* | *required* | `:action` | — |\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'## Defining routes\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'Routes can live on the resource or on the domain. Defining them on the domain is the default recommendation — it keeps resources focused on data and actions while the domain acts as the API surface.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### On the domain\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'defmodule MyApp.Support do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  use Ash.Domain, extensions: [AshJsonApi.Domain]\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  json_api do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    routes do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      base_route "/tickets", MyApp.Support.Ticket do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        get :read\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        index :read\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        post :create\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        patch :update\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        delete :destroy\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'`base_route` scopes all nested routes under the given path prefix for the specified resource.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### On the resource\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'defmodule MyApp.Support.Ticket do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  use Ash.Resource, extensions: [AshJsonApi.Resource]\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  json_api do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    type "ticket"\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    routes do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      base "/tickets"\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      get :read\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      index :read\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      post :create\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      patch :update\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      delete :destroy\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'`base` sets the path prefix for all routes defined on the resource.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'## Standard CRUD routes\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### `get` — fetch a single record\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'get :read\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'Issues a GET request to `/:id` (by default). Looks up a single record by primary key and returns a JSON:API resource object.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### `index` — list records\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +

                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### Anatomy of a Policy\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'Each policy defined in a resource has two parts -\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'- a condition or a list of conditions, such as `action_type(:read)`, `[action_type(:read), actor_attribute_equals(:admin, true)]` or `always()`. If the condition, or all conditions if given a list are true for a given action request, then the policy will be applied to the request.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'- a set of policy checks, each of which will be evaluated individually if a policy applies to a request.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'If more than one policy applies to any given request (eg. an admin actor calls a read action) then **all applicable policies must pass** for the action to be performed.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'A policy will produce one of three results: `:forbidden`, `:authorized`, or `:unknown`. `:unknown` is treated the same as `:forbidden`.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### The Simplest Policy\n'[39m +

                    [32m'  end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'The first argument to `policy` is the condition. In this case, the condition is `always()` - a built-in helper always returning true, meaning that the policy applies to every request.'[39m,

                    [32m'# Routing\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'AshJsonApi provides a set of route helpers that map HTTP requests to Ash actions. Routes are defined inside the `json_api do routes do ... end end` block on either a resource or a domain.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'## Route overview\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'| Route Helper | HTTP Method | Default Path | Primary Action Type | Also Accepts |\n'[39m +
                    [32m'|---|---|---|---|---|\n'[39m +
                    [32m'| `get` | GET | `/:id` | `:read` | `:action` |\n'[39m +
                    [32m'| `index` | GET | `/` | `:read` | `:action` |\n'[39m +
                    [32m'| `post` | POST | `/` | `:create` | `:action`, `:read` |\n'[39m +
                    [32m'| `patch` | PATCH | `/:id` | `:update` | `:action` |\n'[39m +
                    [32m'| `delete` | DELETE | `/:id` | `:destroy` | `:action` |\n'[39m +
                    [32m'| `related` | GET | `/:id/<relationship>` | `:read` | — |\n'[39m +
                    [32m'| `relationship` | GET | `/:id/relationships/<relationship>` | `:read` | — |\n'[39m +
                    [32m'| `post_to_relationship` | POST | `/:id/relationships/<relationship>` | `:update` | — |\n'[39m +
                    [32m'| `patch_relationship` | PATCH | `/:id/relationships/<relationship>` | `:update` | — |\n'[39m +
                    [32m'| `delete_from_relationship` | DELETE | `/:id/relationships/<relationship>` | `:update` | — |\n'[39m +
                    [32m'| `route` | *any* | *required* | `:action` | — |\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'## Defining routes\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'Routes can live on the resource or on the domain. Defining them on the domain is the default recommendation — it keeps resources focused on data and actions while the domain acts as the API surface.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### On the domain\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'defmodule MyApp.Support do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  use Ash.Domain, extensions: [AshJsonApi.Domain]\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  json_api do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    routes do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      base_route "/tickets", MyApp.Support.Ticket do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        get :read\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        index :read\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        post :create\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        patch :update\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        delete :destroy\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'`base_route` scopes all nested routes under the given path prefix for the specified resource.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### On the resource\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'defmodule MyApp.Support.Ticket do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  use Ash.Resource, extensions: [AshJsonApi.Resource]\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  json_api do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    type "ticket"\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    routes do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      base "/tickets"\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      get :read\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      index :read\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      post :create\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      patch :update\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      delete :destroy\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'`base` sets the path prefix for all routes defined on the resource.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'## Standard CRUD routes\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### `get` — fetch a single record\n'[39m +

                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### `index` — list records\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'index :read\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +

                    [32m'Options:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'- `paginate?` (default `true`) — whether to apply pagination\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### `post` — create a record\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +

                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'You can specify which arguments will modify relationships using `relationship_arguments`, but there are some things to keep in mind.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +

                    [32m'If you are not focused on building a fully compliant JSON:API, it is likely far simpler to simply accept arguments\n'[39m +
                    [32m'in the `attributes` key and ignore the `data.relationships` input.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m"If the argument's type is `{:array, _}`, a list of data will be expected. Otherwise, it will expect a single item.\n"[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'Everything in this guide applies to routs defined on the domain as well.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'For example:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'# On a tweets resource\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +

                    [32m'    patch :update, relationship_arguments: [:authors]\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'# And an argument by that name in the action\n'[39m +
                    [32m'actions do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  update :update do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    argument :authors, {:array, :map}, allow_nil?: false\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    change manage_relationship(:authors, type: :append_and_remove) # Use the authors argument to allow changing the related authors on update\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'You can then send the value for `authors` in the relationships key, e.g\n'[39m +

                    [32m'```json\n'[39m +
                    [32m'{\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  data: {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    attributes: {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      ...\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    },\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    relationships: {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      authors: {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        data: [\n'[39m +
                    [32m'          {type: "author", id: 1}, // the `type` key is removed when the value is placed into the action, so this input would be `%{"id" => 1}` (`type` is required by `JSON:API` specification)\n'[39m +
                    [32m'          {type: "author", id: 2, meta: {arbitrary: 1, keys: 2}}, <- `meta` is JSON:API spec freeform data, so this input would be `%{"id" => 2, "arbitrary" => 1, "keys" => 2}`\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        ]\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      }\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    }\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                    [32m'}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +

                    [32m'{\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  data: {\n'[39m +

                    [32m'      authors: {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        {id: 1},\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        {id: 2, arbitrary: 1, keys: 2},\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      }\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    }\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                    [32m'}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'Non-map argument types, e.g `argument :author, :integer` (expecting an author id) work with `manage_relationship`, but not with\n'[39m +
                    [32m'JSON:API, because it expects `{"type": _type, "id" => id}` for relationship values. To support non-map arguments in `relationship_arguments`,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'instead of `:author`, use `{:id, :author}`. This works for `{:array, _}` type arguments as well, so the value would be a list of ids.\n'[39m +

                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'## Creating related resources without the id\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'This feature is useful for creating relationships without requiring two separate API calls and without needing to associate resources with an ID first.                     [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +

                    [32m'# the API\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  json_api do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    routes do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      base_route "/location", Marketplace.Location do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        post :create, relationship_arguments: [:leads]\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      base_route "/lead", Marketplace.Lead do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        post :create\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'# In the leads resource you will have the following:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  actions do\n'[39m +

                    [32m'  # use `patch_relationship` when the operation is both additive and subtractive\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  # use `delete_from_relationship` when the operation is subtractive\n'[39m +
                    [32m'end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +

                    [32m'  change manage_relationship(:author, type: :append)\n'[39m +
